topics.topic: Authority and source for creating or changing OwnerFormField values
questions: Who creates OwnerFormField values, and from what authoritative input are they created for a release?
Which named data provider mints or authors OwnerFormField values, from which exact release artifact or constant, and can any other product action create or change them?
Who creates OwnerFormField values, and from what authoritative input are they created: hand-authored provider data, declared owner-action contracts, page definitions, or generated model metadata?

precedent.topic: Who constructs OwnerFormField values and what source representation or constant contents they use
quotes:
The typed constants of the data closure, the one home of each value the
generated code reads that is neither a setting of the environment
(`runtime_settings`) nor a member of an enumeration or a field's type
(`models`) (SPEC_STANDARD
§6.10, §15.3.1; reopened 2026-11-11, replacing the former
release_declarations module):

`models`, for exactly the row models and enumerations of its eight tables:
`ArtifactTypeOwner` (a type with its owner service) and `ServiceName` for
`ARTIFACT_TYPE_OWNERS`; `ServiceRight` (a service and an operation) with
`ServiceName` and `ServiceOperation` for `SERVICE_RIGHTS`;
`ServiceHighestClass` (a service and its highest class) with `ServiceName`
and `DisclosureClass` for `SERVICE_HIGHEST_CLASSES`; `PersonalDataField` (an
answer model's name and a field's) for `PERSONAL_DATA_FIELDS`;
`RefusalHttpStatus` (a code and its status) with `RefusalCode` for
`REFUSAL_HTTP_STATUSES`; `OwnerActionRoute` (an owner action, its method and
path, whether it is a change and whether it touches an uploaded file) with
`OwnerAction` for `OWNER_ACTIONS`; `OwnerAuditAction` (an owner action,
a customer mark's transition or a project erasure's kind where the action
has one, and the audit action it writes) with `OwnerAction`,
`CustomerTransition`, `ProjectErasure` and `AuditAction` for
`OWNER_AUDIT_ACTIONS`; `OwnerFormField` (an owner form field's name, the
model it fills and how its text is read) with `OwnerFormCarrier` and
`FormValueKind` for `OWNER_FORM_FIELDS`. Its other constants are scalars and import nothing.
precedent.why: State 3 makes OWNER_FORM_FIELDS a typed constant owned by data_provider and makes data_provider depend on the OwnerFormField row model, so the provider constructs and exports OwnerFormField values rather than raw or uninstantiated structural records.

Facts: the field's name; whether it belongs to the request or to its values;

judgement.why: The model lists its fields only as untyped prose even though SPEC_STANDARD §5 requires every field to be stated with its type.

What fact identifies the precise location that the field reads or fills, including nested members and tuple positions, now that path and tuple-position facts are absent?

quotes:
A row's `name` is
the field's name: its path in the `OwnerRequest` or `OwnerValues` it fills
(`carrier`), parts joined by a full stop, with a tuple's position written
where the row holds `OWNER_FORM_POSITION_MARK` (`#`), as decimal digits
from 0.
judgement.why: The later contract makes the name the complete path within the carrier and specifies how tuple positions occur in that path.

quotes:
A row's `name` is
the field's name: its path in the `OwnerRequest` or `OwnerValues` it fills
(`carrier`), parts joined by a full stop, with a tuple's position written
where the row holds `OWNER_FORM_POSITION_MARK` (`#`), as decimal digits
from 0. A row's `reads_as` says how the field's text is read: as the text
itself, an integer's decimal digits, `true` or `false`, or an enumeration
member's value.
judgement.why: The later contract identifies the typed destination by its model path and says a member-valued field produces the destination enumeration's member value, so no separate list identity is left for the generator to guess.

topics.topic: Row identity, field-name namespace, and duplicate-row validity
questions: What makes two occurrences the same field, and may two rows share a field name across pages or destinations?

Is a field occurrence on each page a distinct OwnerFormField, or do equal names across pages denote one shared field; and, if page membership distinguishes them, must the page or owner action be a fact of the model?
What makes two rows rows for the same field, and are duplicate names forbidden globally, forbidden only within a page or destination, or permitted when other facts differ?
Is a field name globally unique across the whole owner interface, unique only within a page or action, or may one globally shared row be reused by several pages?
What duplicate condition makes the owner form table invalid: repeated name, repeated page-and-name, repeated destination path, or only two completely equal rows?

quotes:
Facts: the field's name; whether it belongs to the request or to its values;
how its text is read.
Substitution: two rows with equal facts are the same fact of the table.
judgement.why: OwnerFormField has value identity over the complete declared fact tuple: page or action membership is not an identity fact, equal rows are the same value, and a repeated name with different carrier or reading facts denotes a different value rather than an equal row.

precedent.topic: Which runtime components and owner-interface actions consume OWNER_FORM_FIELDS for rendering, request naming, and submitted-value reading
quotes:
Which action a request names, by its
method and path, and whether it is a change or touches an uploaded file, are
the rows of the data provider's `OWNER_ACTIONS`; its target is the query
parameter `OWNER_TARGET_PARAMETER` names, its CSRF value the form field
`OWNER_CSRF_FIELD` names, every other field it reads or a page writes a row
of `OWNER_FORM_FIELDS` (owner, 2026-11-25), the session cookie's name
`OWNER_SESSION_COOKIE_NAME` and its attributes
`OWNER_SESSION_COOKIE_ATTRIBUTES`, and a page's HTTP status the service API's
`SERVICE_ANSWER_STATUS` and `REFUSAL_HTTP_STATUSES` (owner, 2026-11-24).

Every other field is a row of the
data provider's `OWNER_FORM_FIELDS` (`OwnerFormField`). A row's `name` is
the field's name: its path in the `OwnerRequest` or `OwnerValues` it fills
(`carrier`), parts joined by a full stop, with a tuple's position written
where the row holds `OWNER_FORM_POSITION_MARK` (`#`), as decimal digits
from 0.
precedent.why: The later texts make OWNER_FORM_FIELDS global to every non-target, non-CSRF owner-interface field that a page writes or a request reads, with rows selected by carrier and destination path rather than by a page or action fact.

topics.topic: Which kinds of owner-interface inputs the table exhaustively covers
questions: Is the table a closed, exhaustive set of fields the owner interface may read, and what happens to a submitted or displayed field for which it has no row?
Does OwnerFormField also represent owner-page query inputs, or only form-body inputs?

Does the table contain only visible editable controls, or also query controls and submitted fields the owner does not type or pick, such as ids, revisions, confirmation values, request ids, and CSRF values?

quotes:
The target is the query parameter
`OWNER_TARGET_PARAMETER` (`target`) names, an identity and never a
personal value (R0-29). A `GET` request's other fields are its query's, a
`POST` request's the fields of its `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`
body, or of the upload's multipart head. Every other field is a row of the
data provider's `OWNER_FORM_FIELDS` (`OwnerFormField`).

A field the form leaves out is none,
and a tuple none of whose positions are given is empty. A field whose name
no row names is not read and changes nothing.

The CSRF value is the field
`OWNER_CSRF_FIELD` (`csrf`) names, the upload's first part included, and
`OwnerRequest.csrf_value` carries it from the form's reading to the
request's admission, since a body is read once.
judgement.why: The later contract covers GET query fields and POST body or upload-head fields, excludes target and CSRF into their dedicated constants, and states that an unlisted field is not read and changes nothing.

questions: For repeated controls, tuples, or multi-valued inputs, is there one row for the logical field, one row for each occurrence or position, or is such input outside this model?

questions: Is OwnerFormField a runtime value dataclass instantiated by generated code, or is it structural catalog data represented with a catalog, mapping, or vocabulary kind and omitted from runtime DTO emission?

judgement.why: P1 already judged the unchanged question whether OwnerFormField is a runtime row model instantiated in the provider constant or only non-runtime structural catalog data.

author_guidance: Before editing, identify the decision's owning state from the phase purpose, question_scope and layer obligations, then choose a disposition for each topic that awaits one.
fixed: repair a decision the owning state must make; do not add later-layer implementation choices merely to close a topic. Record the fix commit and review the changed text once.

carried: name the receiving layer and use --what to preserve the choice, its options and consequences, and the required guarantee every option must keep. Decide any guarantee owned here before carrying its execution onward.
accepted: explain why the remaining choice is permitted. Bring an unresolved product choice to the owner with its options and consequences; absence of a quoted requirement does not decide it.
contradiction and standard_violation take no disposition: repair the offending text in its owning state and review the change. Deterministic transition findings must also close through their checks.
